items.why: Course catalog list on the page was refreshed with new AI courses and “New” badges moved; no price or plan change.

The Infrastructure Free card (up to 5 hosts, 1-day retention) was replaced by a Basic host level that can be mixed with Pro or Enterprise hosts, and the free tier is now described in the FAQ as what you move to after the trial.

record.short: The Infrastructure Free card (up to 5 hosts, 1-day metric retention) became a Basic host level, with the free tier now described as the option after the trial ends.
record.headline: Datadog removed the Infrastructure Free card from its pricing page and introduced a Basic host level, while the FAQ says that after the free trial you can move to a Free tier with up to five Basic hosts.
rows: 1-day metric retention on the Free tier
Basic hosts can be mixed with Pro or Enterprise
record.who: Teams using or evaluating the free Infrastructure tier, and paid customers who can now place noncritical hosts on Basic coverage.
record.read: The free tier is no longer a headline plan card but a post-trial landing spot, which pushes evaluators through a trial and positions Basic as a cheaper add-on level for paid accounts.
record.caveat: The page is inconsistent: the Basic card lists 15-month metric retention and a “Contact sales for pricing” line that may belong to the DevSecOps column, while the FAQ says the Free tier has 1-day retention. Basic pricing is not clearly shown.

items.why: Pro button text changed from “Try for $0.00” to “Get started for free”; no price or plan change.

Hosted-agent cache volumes and internal container registry now show as included where they were previously absent for one plan, while the Workflows line shrank from test state management and auto-quarantine to flaky identification and labelling.

record.short: Cache volumes and internal container registry added to more hosted-agent plans, while Workflows now covers flaky identification and labelling instead of test state management and auto-quarantine.

items.why: Only the customer-count claim changed from 350+ to 400+ institutions; no pricing change.
